1.summary: Peter reminds believers that God's power has given them everything for life and godliness, urges them to add virtue upon virtue to their faith, says he will keep reminding them before he dies, and grounds their hope in his eyewitness experience of Christ's majesty on the mountain and in the prophetic word.
1.lookfor: Notice the ladder of virtues in verses 5 to 7, and Peter's memory of the transfiguration.

names.name: Simon Peter
names.gloss: The apostle, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ.

insights.title: Everything we need
insights.body: His divine power has granted us everything for life and godliness (1:3). Growth isn't about acquiring something missing but living out what we've been given.

insights.title: Partakers of the divine nature
insights.body: Through his promises you may become partakers of the divine nature (1:4). Not becoming God, but sharing his life and character, escaping corruption.

insights.title: Add to your faith
insights.body: Add to faith virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, godliness, brotherly affection and love (1:5-7). The list climbs like a staircase, from faith to love.

insights.title: Putting off the tent
insights.body: Peter knows that the putting off of his tent will come soon, as the Lord Jesus showed him (1:14). Jesus had told Peter he would die stretched out by others.

insights.title: On the holy mountain
insights.body: We didn't follow clever myths; we were eyewitnesses of his majesty, and heard the voice: this is my beloved Son (1:16-18). Peter recalls the transfiguration.

insights.title: Carried along by the Spirit
insights.body: No prophecy came by human will, but holy men spoke from God, moved by the Holy Spirit (1:21). The word for moved is used of a ship carried by the wind.

insights.title: A lamp in a dark place
insights.body: The prophetic word is like a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts (1:19).

insights.title: Reminders
insights.body: Peter says he'll keep reminding them of what they already know (1:12). What truth do you need to be reminded of today?

2.summary: Peter warns of false teachers who will secretly bring in destructive heresies, deny the Master who bought them, and exploit people with greed and sensuality; God judged angels, the ancient world and Sodom while rescuing Noah and Lot, so he knows how to rescue the godly and judge the wicked.
2.lookfor: Notice the three examples of judgment and the two of rescue, and the vivid descriptions of the false teachers.

names.name: Noah
names.gloss: A preacher of righteousness, preserved through the flood.

names.name: Sodom
names.gloss: A city destroyed for its wickedness.

names.name: Gomorrah
names.gloss: Sodom's neighbor city, destroyed with it.

names.name: Balaam
names.gloss: A prophet hired to curse Israel, who loved the wages of wickedness.

insights.title: Denying the Master
insights.body: False teachers deny the Master who bought them (2:1). The image is of slaves turning against the owner who paid for their freedom.

insights.title: Three judgments
insights.body: God didn't spare angels who sinned, didn't spare the ancient world but preserved Noah, and turned Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes but rescued Lot (2:4-7). Judgment and rescue together.

insights.title: Tartarus
insights.body: God cast sinning angels down to Tartarus (2:4), the Greek name for the deepest pit of the underworld. It appears only here in the Bible.

insights.title: Righteous Lot?
insights.body: Peter calls Lot righteous, tormented by what he saw in Sodom (2:7-8). Genesis shows Lot's many failings; Peter sees that he still belonged to God and was grieved by evil.

insights.title: Balaam's donkey
insights.body: They follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing and was rebuked by a mute donkey speaking with a human voice (2:15-16).

insights.title: Springs without water
insights.body: These are springs without water, mists driven by a storm (2:17). They promise refreshment and deliver nothing; they promise freedom while themselves slaves of corruption (2:19).

insights.title: The Lord knows how to rescue
insights.body: The Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous for judgment (2:9). The chapter's warnings rest on this assurance.

insights.title: Spotting falsehood
insights.body: Peter says false teachers exploit with greed and promise freedom. What helps you tell sound teaching from teaching that only flatters?

3.summary: Peter answers scoffers who say nothing has changed since creation: God's timing differs from ours, his patience gives time for repentance, and the day of the Lord will come like a thief, bringing new heavens and a new earth; so live holy lives, be at peace, beware of distorting Scripture, and grow in grace.
3.lookfor: Notice why God seems slow, and Peter's comment on Paul's letters.

names.name: Paul
names.gloss: Our beloved brother, whose letters some found hard to understand.

insights.title: Where is his coming?
insights.body: Scoffers ask, where is the promise of his coming? Since the fathers fell asleep, everything continues as from creation (3:4). Peter answers that they forget the flood.

insights.title: A thousand years
insights.body: With the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day (3:8), echoing Psalm 90. God doesn't live in our hurry.

insights.title: Not slow but patient
insights.body: The Lord isn't slow about his promise, as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wanting any to perish but all to come to repentance (3:9). The delay is mercy.

insights.title: The elements melt
insights.body: The heavens will pass away with a roar, the elements melt with fervent heat, and the earth and its works will be laid bare (3:10). Some manuscripts read burned up; laid bare suggests exposed before God.

insights.title: New heavens and a new earth
insights.body: We look for new heavens and a new earth in which righteousness dwells (3:13), as Isaiah promised. The end is renewal, not mere destruction.

insights.title: Hard things in Paul
insights.body: Paul's letters contain some things hard to understand, which the ignorant twist, as they do the other Scriptures (3:15-16). Paul's letters are already set beside Scripture.

insights.title: Grow in grace
insights.body: The letter ends: grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ (3:18). Peter's last recorded words are about growth.

insights.title: God's patience
insights.body: Peter says God's patience means salvation (3:15). Whose salvation are you praying for while God waits?

intro.who: Simon Peter (1:1), writing as his death approaches (1:14). Many scholars think a follower wrote it in his name after his death, since its style differs from 1 Peter and it was slow to be widely accepted; others defend Peter's authorship.
intro.when: If by Peter, about AD 64–67, shortly before his death in Rome; otherwise perhaps AD 80–100.
intro.why: False teachers were mocking the promise of Christ's return and using freedom as an excuse for immorality. The letter, like a last testament, urges believers to grow in godliness, trust the apostles' eyewitness testimony and the prophets, and wait patiently for the day of the Lord.

outline.title: Growing in godliness; eyewitness and prophecy
The day of the Lord will come
